thread:
Alex: Heads up — saw a notable drop in prefix/prompt cache hit-rate on Private today vs Hosted. Profiling attached (high-level numbers below).

Morgan: Numbers?

Alex: Hosted: ~78% hit-rate over last 24h. Private (customer-vpc): ~52%.
Warmup tail increased, cold token latency up ~1.6x for affected sequences.

Priya: Any recent prompt/template changes? Keying normalization?

Alex: We rolled a minor templating change last week that inserts `metadata: <env>` header into prompts for audit. That looks like it might be in the cache key.

Diego: Also worth noting: Private uses an NFS mount for the persistent KV store for that customer (policy reasons) vs local SSD for Hosted. NFS latency and jitter increased observed RPS for KV operations — could reduce effective hit-rate if we time out or fall back.

Alex: Example of current key we see in logs: `prefix_key:v1|model:gptx|prompt_hash:84a2f|meta:env=staging|reqid=abc123` — note `reqid` and `meta` are included.

Morgan: Oof. `reqid` should never be part of the cache key. That explains a huge portion of entropy. Priya — why did the templating change add `meta`?

Priya: It was added to the rendered prompt for observability but we mistakenly used the rendered prompt blob as the sole key input rather than canonicalized template+slots. We intended to canonicalize but didn't.

DeployBot: Canary rollout 2026-03-16T10:12Z completed for template-change. No automated rollback triggered. :white_check_mark:

Diego: Two separate effects here: 1) keying entropy from metadata/reqid, 2) storage/backing store differences — NFS adds latency and increases apparent misses since some reads time out and we fallback to model compute. Also batching heuristics differ across deployment modes: Hosted continuous-batcher latency target = 5ms => more coalescing of identical prefixes in-flight, Private had a conservative 20ms target in this customer's config so fewer in-flight duplicates to hit cache or KV TTL windows.

Alex: Repro plan proposed: 
- Run a dedicated sim that renders prompts both with and without `meta`/`reqid` in keying.
- Set `REDWOOD_CACHE_KEY_NORMALIZE=1` locally (feature flag) to canonicalize template+slots and compare hit-rates.
- Run with `--kv-backend=local` vs `--kv-backend=nfs` to measure KV op latency contribution.

Morgan: Commands for repro (copyable):
```
# local canonicalization toggle
export REDWOOD_CACHE_KEY_NORMALIZE=1
# sim runner
./tools/prefix-sim --model=gptx --scenario=customer-vpc --qps=200 --duration=900
# kv backends
./tools/kvbench --backend=local --rps=500
./tools/kvbench --backend=nfs --rps=500
```

Priya: For a quick mitigation we can: 1) revert the templating change that injects `meta` into the rendered prompt OR 2) change keying so we derive the cache key from `template_id + canonicalized_slots` (no rendered blobs). Option 2 is safer long-term.

Diego: Also suggest lowering Private's batch latency from 20ms -> 8ms for a short A/B to see effect on coalescing. Batching parameter lives in `runtime.batch.latency_ms`.

Alex: I ran a tiny local run with `REDWOOD_CACHE_KEY_NORMALIZE=1` and hit-rate jumped from 53% -> 74% in 30 minutes. KV latencies still matter but key entropy was the big win.

Morgan: OK plan of action: 
- Priya to push keying fix (template_id + canonical slots) behind a flag by EOD.
- Diego to run batch-latency A/B on one Private cluster and run kvbench with NFS TTLs adjusted.
- Alex will prepare a short rollback/runbook if the fix causes regressions.

Priya: I created a minimal change: `cache/keyer: use TemplateKeyer` PR in draft, includes tests and a toggle `enable_template_keyer`. Will link.

DeployBot: Test canary started for `enable_template_keyer` flag on staging.

Alex: Great. Also we should add a lint rule to fail CI if `reqid` or other ephemeral fields are present in the key derivation function.

Morgan: Agree. After fixes, target: >70% prefix hit-rate on Private and Hosted parity within ±5%. Otherwise we evaluate KV/backing optimization (SSD option or replicate small hotset locally).

Diego: Note for docs/ops — VPC customers who require NFS/remote KV should be on a different recommended config (smaller TTLs for in-memory cache, local hotset replication). I'll draft recommended config.

Alex: Thanks all — I'll collect profiling artifacts and share a short summary in #eng-runtime after the roll. :eyes:
